claims: The Fab Five were the 1991 University of Michigan men’s basketball recruiting class.
The Fab Five consisted of Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
The Fab Five became the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach an NCAA Championship game.
The Fab Five reached consecutive Final Fours in 1992 and 1993.
Jimmy King was from Plano, Texas.
Ray Jackson was from Austin, Texas.
The Fab Five started all games as freshmen in 1992.
The Fab Five lost to Duke 71-51 in the 1992 NCAA final.
The Fab Five lost to North Carolina 77-71 in 1993.
Chris Webber received a technical foul for calling a timeout that did not exist in the 1993 game against North Carolina.
The 1992 and 1993 Final Four appearances of the Fab Five were later vacated due to their association with a University of Michigan booster scandal.
Four members of the Fab Five reached the NBA.
Juwan Howard won two NBA championships with the Miami Heat.
Chris Webber was an NBA All-Star with the Sacramento Kings.
The Fab Five reunited for a special alt-cast of the 2026 Michigan-Arizona Final Four game on truTV and HBO Max.
